senses.gloss:
मुगदस मुगदस, मुगदेमु, मुगल-स्था-
न, names of places.

मुगूह मुगूह, अस्, m. a species of gallinule
(= दात्यूह).
मुग्ध मुग्ध, &c. See under rt. 1. मुह्.

मुग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, perplexed, stupid,
ignorant; infatuated, enamoured; foolish, silly, sim-
ple, mistaken, erring; inexperienced, artless, inno-
cent, rendered attractive by youthful simplicity,
charming, tender, lovely, beautiful; (आ), f. a young
and beautiful female.
—मुग्ध-कथा, f. a story
of a fool, tale about a fool.
—मुग्ध-ता, f. or
मुग्ध-त्व, अम्, n. stupidity, silliness, ignorance;
simplicity, artlessness, loveliness, charmingness, grace-
fulness.
—मुग्ध-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, lovely-eyed, hav-
ing beautiful eyes.
—मुग्ध-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, or
मुग्ध-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, silly, simple, a simpleton.
—मुग्ध-बोध, अम्, n. ‘instructing the igno-
rant’ (scil. व्याकरण), N. of a celebrated grammar
by Vopa-deva (a grammarian who is supposed to
have flourished in the thirteenth century, and who is
regarded as a great authority in Bengal).
—मुग्ध-
बोध-परिशिष्ट, अम्, n. a supplement or appendix
to the Mugdha-bodha.
—मुग्धबोध-प्रदीप,
अस्, m., N. of a commentary on the Mugdha-bodha.
—मुग्धबोध-सम्बोधिनी, f., N. of a com-
mentary on the Mugdha-bodha.
—मुग्ध-बोधिनी,
f., scil. टीका, N. of a commentary by Bharata-malla
on the Amara-koṣa and of a commentary by Bha-
rata-mallika (probably identical with the preceding
author) on the Bhaṭṭi-kāvya.
—मुग्ध-भाव, अस्,
m. stupidity, simplicity, inexperience.
—मुग्ध-
वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, perplexed, embarrassed, infatuated,
mistaken.
—मुग्धाक्षी (˚ध-अक्˚), f. a lovely-
eyed woman.
—मुग्धाग्रणी (˚ध-अग्˚), ईस्, m.
the greatest of simpletons, the stupidest of the stupid.
—मुग्धा-चक्र, अम्, n. a particular mystical
circle.
—मुग्धानन (˚ध-आन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
lovely-faced.
